title: Punjab Urban Land Systems Enhancement Project (PULSE)
client: Board of Revenue Punjab / Punjab Land Records Authority
map_scope_note: The Lahore pin is a city-level reference marker. PULSE is province-wide; this map does not show its full coverage or project boundaries.
summary: PULSE is a province-wide programme to modernise land administration in Punjab. It is developing digital land records and a seamless cadastral map linked to the Land Records Management Information System, covering rural and urban land. The programme includes digitising remaining manual mouzas, georeferencing revenue maps (musavi), mapping parcels, linking maps to land records and checking spatial-data quality across the province.
delivered: Digitisation of remaining manual mouzas
Georeferencing of revenue maps (musavi) and parcel mapping
Linking parcel maps to land records
Spatial-data quality assurance

title: Punjab Spatial Strategy
client: Planning and Development Department, Government of the Punjab; executing agency: The Urban Unit
funding: World Bank (Punjab Jobs and Competitiveness Program for Results)
map_scope_note: The Lahore pin is a city-level reference marker. The strategy covers Punjab; this map does not show its full study area or project boundaries.
summary: The Punjab Spatial Strategy provides a long-term framework for assessing the province's growth corridors and economic nodes and guiding public investment in infrastructure and industry. It brought together province-wide information on administrative boundaries down to mouza level, land cover and use, utilities, topography, industries, transport, water and public facilities. The work produced spatial analyses and knowledge products, including the Map Book of the Punjab.
delivered: Primary and secondary GIS data collection
Spatial analysis and knowledge products
The Map Book of the Punjab

title: GIS Based Urban Immovable Property Tax System (UIPT)
client: Excise and Taxation Department, Punjab; executing agency: The Urban Unit
location_label: Lahore, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Rawalpindi, Multan and Sialkot, Punjab
map_scope_note: Pins mark the six cities listed for this project. They are city-level references, not parcel-level tax maps.
summary: This project computerised urban property tax and integrated it with GIS. After a pilot in Sialkot, the system was extended to five large districts that account for most of Punjab's property-tax demand. Property registers were scanned, parcels were digitised on satellite imagery, and field-survey records and property photographs were linked to a tax database. The system supported automated assessments and generation of demand notices.
delivered: Digitised property parcels for five districts
Door-to-door survey data linked to GIS
Scanned PT-1 and PT-8 registers
Automated tax calculation and PT-10 demand notices

title: Automation of Wheat Procurement System
client: United Bank Limited and Food Department, Government of the Punjab; executing agency: The Urban Unit
map_scope_note: This is a locality marker for the Dunyapur pilot, not a mapped field boundary.
summary: This pilot combined GIS and information technology to make wheat procurement and grower payments more transparent. Musavis for the tehsil were scanned and digitised on high-resolution satellite imagery, and growers were registered against their land parcels. Remote sensing was used to estimate wheat-growing area to support yield forecasting and procurement decisions. The resulting work included digitised parcels linked to records of rights, a grower database and a decision-support system.
delivered: Digitised land parcels linked to records of rights
Wheat-area estimation using remote sensing
Grower database and decision-support system

title: Asset Management of Pakistan Railways Land (GIS-based computerisation and MIS database)
client: Pakistan Railways; executing agency: The Urban Unit
map_scope_note: Pins mark the listed city-level references, not the extent of railway land or surveyed boundaries.
summary: This project developed a database and imagery view of Pakistan Railways land, harmonised with provincial revenue records so the status of land blocks could be queried. Revenue maps were collected, scanned, georeferenced and digitised, with physical surveys also carried out. In unsettled areas without revenue records, new musavis were constructed using adjacent mouza boundaries, DGPS surveys and tape measurements with revenue staff; boundary pillars were installed as reference marks.
delivered: Georeferenced and digitised cadastral maps
Newly constructed musavis for unsettled areas
Land dashboard covering records, land use and encroachments

title: Scanning and Preservation of Punjab Land Revenue Record in Flood-Affected Districts
client: Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) Punjab; executing agency: The Urban Unit
location_label: DG Khan, Muzaffargarh, Rajanpur, Layyah, Rahim Yar Khan, Bhakkar and Bahawalpur, Punjab
map_scope_note: District-level reference markers for the listed flood-affected districts; the map does not show record coverage or cadastral boundaries.
summary: After the 2010 floods damaged fragile paper cadastral maps, this project digitised land-revenue records from seven affected districts to preserve them and support integration with Punjab's spatial data infrastructure. The work described in the source material includes scanning, mosaicking, georeferencing and digitising the maps. The reference period of April to November 2011 predates Farkhanda's July 2012 start date, so her involvement dates are left unreported pending confirmation.
delivered: Scanning and mosaicking of land-revenue maps
Georeferencing and digitisation of maps from seven districts
Digital preservation and integration with spatial data infrastructure
